fixes.summary: Centralize tolerance validation in one helper in common.rs that rejects NaN, +/-Inf and negative rtol/atol with CoreError::InvalidInput, and a second helper that builds the stopping threshold and rejects a non-finite result (rtol*||b|| can overflow even when both tolerances are finite). GmresConfig::validate calls the first helper; LgmresConfig and GcrodrConfig gain a validate() (today lgmres.rs:58-62 and gcrodr.rs:401-407 check only iteration/dimension limits, no tolerance check at all) that is called before validate_system, and GcrodrConfig additionally requires rank_tol finite and in (0,1). The three `config.atol.max(config.rtol * right_norm)` sites are replaced by the threshold helper, and the ad hoc duplicate checks in gmres_givens.rs:304-318 collapse onto the same helpers so all five kernels fail closed identically before any operator work.
fixes.verification: New table-driven test krylov_contracts.rs::scalar_kernels_reject_non_finite_or_negative_tolerances: for each of solve_gmres, solve_lgmres, solve_gcrodr, solve_gmres_givens and each of rtol/atol in {NaN, +Inf, -Inf, -1.0} on a 4x4 nonsingular diagonal system, assert Err(CoreError::InvalidInput(_)), assert WorkCounters is unchanged (linear_matvecs == 0, preconditioner_apps == 0, linear_solves == 0) and that LGMRES/GCRO-DR state equals its pre-call snapshot. Second test threshold_overflow_is_rejected: rtol=1e300 with ||b||=1e10 must return InvalidInput rather than Ok(converged=true, x=0). Regression guard: atol=0.0 with finite rtol (the E-05 configuration) must still converge; existing givens test candidate_rejects_non_finite_tolerances_before_operator_work (givens_gmres_contracts.rs:390) must stay green.

fixes.summary: LinearSolverConfig::validate (solver_types.rs:54-57) has the same sign-only check, so the integrator-level gate at sequential.rs:301 passes NaN/Inf tolerances down to every kernel. Make the core check `is_finite() && >= 0.0` for rtol and atol (recycle_rank_tol is already NaN-safe through its negated range test at :64). Because sequential.rs:402-407 builds GmresConfig from derived linear_rtol/linear_atol rather than from the validated config fields, the kernel-side validation from the previous fix stays as the second line of defence; do not remove either layer.
fixes.verification: Unit test in rodas5p-core solver_types.rs tests: linear_solver_config_rejects_non_finite_tolerances iterates rtol/atol over {NaN, +Inf, -Inf, -0.5} and asserts validate() is Err with a message containing 'finite'; default config and rtol=0/atol=0 boundary stay Ok. Integrator-level test: a step with LinearMethod::Gmres and atol=f64::INFINITY returns CoreError::InvalidInput and leaves WorkCounters at zero.

fixes.summary: Replace the unconditional success return in the degenerate-seed branch of solve_seeded_gmres (block_gmres.rs:493-511) with the same certificate the rank-0 block path uses at :301-313. With x=0 the true residual is exactly b_i, so no operator application is needed: set residual_norms[i]=safe_l2(b_i), compare against atol.max(rtol*||b_i||), and return CoreError::LinearSolve naming the annihilated RHS when any row fails; only a block whose rows genuinely satisfy their thresholds (all-zero RHS, or ||b_i|| <= atol) returns Ok, and then with honest residual norms instead of fabricated zeros. Also guard a non-finite seed_norm with CoreError::NonFinite, since max_by with total_cmp orders NaN above every finite norm, so a NaN row is selected as the seed, and `NaN <= MIN_POSITIVE` is false, which would otherwise normalize the seed by NaN.
fixes.verification: Three new tests in block_gmres_contracts.rs. (1) seeded_gmres_rejects_preconditioner_that_annihilates_nonzero_rhs: a test-local ZeroingPreconditioner whose apply fills y with 0.0, two nonzero RHS rows, default tolerances; assert Err(CoreError::LinearSolve(_)) and that counters.linear_solves and counters.block_linear_solves are unchanged. (2) seeded_gmres_zero_rhs_block_is_certified_with_true_residuals: all-zero RHS rows return Ok with residual_norms all 0.0 and solutions all zero. (3) seeded_gmres_degenerate_seed_reports_true_norms_under_loose_atol: same ZeroingPreconditioner with atol larger than every ||b_i|| returns Ok with residual_norms[i] == safe_l2(b_i), not 0.0. Add one doc sentence on Preconditioner (operator.rs:286) stating that implementations are not assumed nonsingular and that kernels certify on the unpreconditioned residual.

fixes.summary: Stop using the non-production kernel as calibration evidence. scientific_corpus_v2_spectral_contracts.rs:244-258 calls solve_gmres_givens as its matrix-free GMRES probe, while production dispatch at sequential.rs:401-419 only ever calls solve_gmres / solve_gmres_with_residual_scale. Switch the probe to solve_gmres with the identical GmresConfig, re-derive the pinned iteration counts from the production kernel, and if the Givens numbers are still wanted keep them as a second, explicitly labelled column rather than as the corpus authority.
fixes.verification: After the switch, `grep -rn solve_gmres_givens crates/rodas5p-integrators` returns no hit in a test that produces corpus calibration values. The spectral contract test must pass with iteration counts regenerated from solve_gmres; any pinned dimension-sensitivity value that moves is recorded in the corpus changelog as a kernel-provenance correction. Risk is medium only because pinned expectations may shift and need re-baselining.

fixes.summary: Make the kernel's status and its divergence from gmres.rs an explicit, tested contract instead of an accident. Add module docs to gmres_givens.rs stating it is a research candidate with no production caller (the report already says method "gmres-givens-candidate" at :497) and listing the three deliberate differences: fail-closed on a rejected happy-breakdown candidate (:436-441) where gmres.rs breaks the cycle and restarts (:181-183, loop at :218), rejection of a rank-deficient triangular factor at 100*eps*max|R_ii| (:214-226) where gmres.rs solves a small least-squares problem each step (:177-180), and the heuristic projected trigger threshold*beta/||r_true|| (:368-374). Gate the public re-export in lib.rs:26-30 behind a non-default cargo feature (for example `research-kernels`) enabled by the krylov test targets, so no integrator, fair-ab or CLI crate can adopt it without an explicit opt-in.
fixes.verification: New differential test givens_gmres_contracts.rs::candidate_and_production_outcomes_are_pinned_on_nonnormal_jacobi: build the E-05 s=1 nonnormal operator (A=Q(D+N)Q^T, n=256, Jacobi preconditioner) at RHS scales 1e-14, 1, 1e14 with the E-05 budget, run both solve_gmres and solve_gmres_givens, and assert (a) whenever both return Ok, each solution independently satisfies the same recomputed true-residual threshold, and (b) the Ok/Err outcome pair per row equals a pinned table (E-05 observed gmres ok/fail/ok versus givens fail/ok/fail, from $RUN/exp/E-05/e05_raw.json), so any future change to either kernel's success semantics breaks the test visibly. Build check: `cargo build -p rodas5p-integrators -p rodas5p-fair-ab -p rodas5p-cli` without the feature must succeed, proving no production crate depends on the kernel.

fixes.summary: Remove the accounting asymmetry that makes cost comparisons between the two kernels unsound. gmres.rs charges its per-restart true-residual evaluation as ApplyCategory::Krylov (:228), so it is inside report.matvecs, whereas certify_candidate in gmres_givens.rs charges every in-cycle certification, including rejected ones, as ApplyCategory::Diagnostic (:281) and the report takes matvecs from delta.linear_matvecs (:495). Charge in-cycle certifications that gate termination as Krylov work (keeping only the final post-loop certificate at :478 as Diagnostic, matching gmres.rs:282), and surface projected_residual_checks / rejected_projected_residual_checks from GmresGivensStatistics next to the matvec count in any comparison output. Until this lands, no claim that projected-residual termination reduces production cost should cite this kernel.
fixes.verification: Extend rejected_projected_triggers_back_off_diagnostics_but_stay_certified (givens_gmres_contracts.rs:169): with a counting operator, assert report.matvecs == total operator applications minus exactly one (the final certificate), i.e. every rejected in-cycle certification is included. Re-run experiment E-05 and confirm the gmres_givens matvec column rises by the number of rejected checks while reported/recomputed residual ratios remain within 1 +/- 2e-15. Risk is medium because pinned matvec counts in existing Givens contract tests will change.
